title: Rational cohomology coactions from a quasi-coherent sheaf linearization
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $G$ an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $Y$ a quasi-compact separated $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $a:G\times_kY\to Y$ be a left action, with identity and associativity as morphism equalities. Let $\mathcal E$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] with a $G$-linearization: an isomorphism $\theta:p_2^*\mathcal E\to a^*\mathcal E$ [def-pc-module-pullback] restricting to the identity at the group identity, and satisfying $\theta_{gh,y}=\theta_{g,hy}\theta_{h,y}$ on $G\times_kG\times_kY$. This equation means equality of the pulled-back sheaf maps, not just equality at field-valued points. A map of linearized sheaves is a sheaf map commuting with $\theta$. Write $H^i(Y,\mathcal E)$ for right-derived global sections on Zariski module sheaves [pqf-def-cohomology], with its $k$-vector-space structure. For every $i\geq0$ there is a canonical coaction $$c_i:H^i(Y,\mathcal E)\longrightarrow H^i(Y,\mathcal E)\otimes_k k[G]$$ satisfying $(c_i\otimes1)c_i=(1\otimes\Delta)c_i$ and $(1\otimes\varepsilon)c_i=1$, where $\Delta,\varepsilon$ are induced by multiplication and identity of $G$. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ the canonical map $A\otimes_k H^i(Y,\mathcal E)\to H^i(Y_A,\mathcal E_A)$, $b\otimes z\mapsto b\,p^*z$, is an isomorphism; under it evaluation of $c_i$ at any $g\in G(A)$ is the cohomological action induced by $g$ and $\theta$. In degree zero it sends a section $s$ to the section with value $(g s)(y)=\theta_{g,g^{-1}y}(s(g^{-1}y))$. These coactions are natural in maps of linearized sheaves. For a short exact sequence of linearized quasi-coherent modules, every map, including every connecting map, of its natural long exact Zariski cohomology sequence is a homomorphism of these $k[G]$-comodules. No properness, coherence, finite-dimensionality of cohomology, smoothness or reductivity of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology (the canonical flat base-change isomorphism). The coaction and compatibility with connecting maps are an agent-written consequence using the universal group element and naturality of right-derived global sections; not a verbatim assertion of 02KH.

proof.text: Put $V_i=H^i(Y,\mathcal E)$. Every $k$-module is flat [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], so every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ is a flat $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat: each of its stalks is a vector space over $k$, which is precisely the stalkwise definition [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The scheme $Y$ is quasi-compact and its structure morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated, and $\mathcal E$ is quasi-coherent. Hence [lem-pc-flat-cohomology-separated], with $R=k$ and $S=A$, says that the specific comparison $\beta^i_{Y,\mathcal E,A}:A\otimes_k\operatorname{HOver}(Y,\mathcal E,i)\to\operatorname{HOver}(Y_A,\mathcal E_A,i)$, $a\otimes x\mapsto a\cdot p_A^*x$, of [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison] is bijective; an abstract isomorphism would not suffice, since steps 4 to 8 compute with this formula. That comparison is written in the Ext model of cohomology. By [new-module-cohomology-ext-pullback-comparison] (with $R=k$, $B=A$, $h:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$) there are additive equivalences $E$ on $Y$ and $E'$ on $Y_A$ from right-derived module cohomology to the Ext model, natural in module morphisms, with $E'(p_A^*z)=\operatorname{baseChangeLinear}(E(z))$, where $p_A^*$ is the module-cohomology pullback of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (a). Naturality for the module endomorphisms given by multiplication by global functions makes $E$ $k$-linear and $E'$ $A$-linear. Transporting along $1\otimes E$ and $E'$, the map $\beta_A^i:A\otimes_kV_i\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(Y_A,\mathcal E_A)$, $a\otimes z\mapsto a\,p_A^*z$, is bijective, with $p_A^*$ the f-map pullback used in steps 2 to 8. This works for every commutative $k$-algebra, including the zero algebra; the latter has empty spectrum and both sides vanish.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology (2), and the specified comparison in its proof (separated finite-affine-cover case)

proof.text: For $g\in G(A)$ let $a_g:Y_A\to Y_A$ be the action automorphism and set $t_g=a_{g^{-1}}$. Restrict $\theta$ along $(g,\operatorname{id})$ to get $\theta_g:\mathcal E_A\to a_g^*\mathcal E_A$. Pull it back by $t_g$ and use $a_g t_g=\operatorname{id}$ to obtain $q_g:t_g^*\mathcal E_A\to\mathcal E_A$. Define $$r_A^i(g)=H^i(q_g)\circ t_g^*:H^i(Y_A,\mathcal E_A)\to H^i(Y_A,\mathcal E_A).$$ Here pullback and its coefficient map mean exactly [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], with the canonical pullback composition identifications [def-pc-module-pullback]. The linearity and degree-zero assertions of [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-basic-properties] show that $r_A^i(g)$ is $A$-linear and, for sections, sends $s$ to $y\mapsto\theta_{g,g^{-1}y}s(g^{-1}y)$. This formula denotes the pulled-back sheaf map, so it does not assume that sections or morphisms are detected by field-valued points.

source.place: Tag 01F7, functoriality of cohomology; agent-written universal-element construction

proof.text: The given sheaf cocycle identity, pulled back along $(g,h,(gh)^{-1}y)$, gives $$t_{gh}=t_h\circ t_g,\qquad q_{gh}=q_g\circ t_g^*(q_h),\qquad q_e=\operatorname{id}.$$ Indeed the two coefficient factors are $\theta_{g,g^{-1}y}$ and $\theta_{h,h^{-1}g^{-1}y}$, in that order. The composition and coefficient-naturality clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] therefore give $r_A^i(g)r_A^i(h)=r_A^i(gh)$; the identity clause of [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-basic-properties] gives $r_A^i(e)=1$. Thus these are actions, with inverse $r_A^i(g^{-1})$. All equalities used here are sheaf-map equalities pulled back from the given cocycle.

source.place: Tag 01F7, functoriality of cohomology; agent-written universal-element construction

proof.text: For a $k$-algebra map $\alpha:A\to A'$ let $b:Y_{A'}\to Y_A$. Functoriality and the scalar law [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial, lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-basic-properties] give, on pure tensors, $$b^*\beta_A^i(a\otimes z)=\alpha(a)p_{A'}^*z=\beta_{A'}^i(\alpha(a)\otimes z).$$ Moreover $t_g b=b t_{\alpha(g)}$ and $b^*q_g=q_{\alpha(g)}$ under the composition identifications, since all were obtained by pulling back the same action and linearization maps. Applying the same composition and coefficient-naturality laws gives $$b^*r_A^i(g)=r_{A'}^i(\alpha(g))b^*.$$ No flatness of $\alpha$ is needed: these are cohomology f-maps, not an application of flat base change over $A$. The two $\beta$ isomorphisms come independently from the field $k$.

source.place: Tag 01F7, functoriality of cohomology; agent-written universal-element construction

proof.text: Set $B=k[G]$ and let $u\in G(B)$ be the universal element, namely the identity morphism of the affine scheme $G$. Define $c_i(z)$ by applying $r_B^i(u)$ to $\beta_B^i(1\otimes z)$, then $(\beta_B^i)^{-1}$, then the tensor flip $B\otimes_kV_i\cong V_i\otimes_kB$. For any $g\in G(A)$ let $\operatorname{ev}_g:B\to A$ be its coordinate map. Step 4 with $\alpha=\operatorname{ev}_g$ proves that evaluation of $c_i(z)$ is $(\beta_A^i)^{-1}r_A^i(g)\beta_A^i(1\otimes z)$ (with the tensor flip understood). Both resulting operators are $A$-linear, so agreement on $1\otimes z$ is agreement on $A\otimes V_i$. This proves the stated evaluation assertion and identifies degree zero with the formula in step 2. The construction uses the actual universal element and the canonical $\beta$, and hence specifies a canonical linear map into the algebraic tensor product.

source.place: Tag 01F7, functoriality of cohomology; agent-written universal-element construction

proof.text: Use $D=B\otimes_kB$ and the two universal elements $u_1,u_2\in G(D)$, obtained from the first and second inclusions of $B$. In $V_i\otimes_kD$, step 5 identifies $(1\otimes\Delta)c_i(z)$ with $r_D^i(u_1u_2)(1\otimes z)$. To compute the other side write $c_i(z)=\sum_j z_j\otimes b_j$. After evaluation at $(u_1,u_2)$, $(c_i\otimes1)c_i(z)=\sum_j c_i(z_j)\otimes b_j$ corresponds to $r_D^i(u_1)r_D^i(u_2)(1\otimes z)$: the second action contributes the $b_j$ in the second $B$ factor and the first action contributes $c_i(z_j)$ in the first. Step 3 makes these equal. Evaluation at this universal pair is the identity on the coordinate ring $D$, so this is equality of tensors, with no density assertion. Likewise evaluation at $e\in G(k)$ is $1\otimes\varepsilon$ and step 3 gives $(1\otimes\varepsilon)c_i=1$. These are the required two coaction laws.

source.place: Tag 01F7, functoriality of cohomology; agent-written universal-element construction

proof.text: If $v:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$ is a map of linearized sheaves, its pullbacks satisfy $v_Aq_g^{\mathcal E}=q_g^{\mathcal F}t_g^*(v_A)$. The coefficient-naturality laws of [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] then make $H^i(v_A)$ commute with $r_A^i(g)$. Also $H^i(v_A)\beta_A^{i,\mathcal E}=\beta_A^{i,\mathcal F}(1\otimes H^i(v))$, by the formula for $\beta$ and that same naturality. Apply these equations with $A=B$ and $g=u$ to obtain $(H^i(v)\otimes1)c_i^{\mathcal E}=c_i^{\mathcal F}H^i(v)$. This proves naturality, and already covers the maps at fixed degree in any short exact sequence.

source.place: Tag 01F7, functoriality of cohomology; agent-written universal-element construction

proof.text: Let $E$ be the given short exact linearized sequence. Each $p_A:Y_A\to Y$ is flat by step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]; hence its module pullback is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective], giving a short exact row $E_A$. Apply [lem-sfb-module-cohomology-fmap-boundary] to the unit coefficient maps over $p_A$ to get $p_A^{i+1}\delta_E^i=\delta_{E_A}^ip_A^i$. Apply it over the identity to multiplication by any $a\in A$ on all three terms of $E_A$: thus $\delta_{E_A}^i$ is $A$-linear. The pure-tensor formula for $\beta_A$ now gives $$\delta_{E_A}^i\beta_A^{i,E_3}=\beta_A^{i+1,E_1}(1\otimes\delta_E^i).$$ Apply the same boundary lemma with $f=t_g:Y_A\to Y_A$ and the three coefficient maps adjoint to $q_g^{E_j}$. Their squares commute by linearization-equivariance of the arrows of $E$. It gives $\delta_{E_A}^i r_A^{i,E_3}(g)=r_A^{i+1,E_1}(g)\delta_{E_A}^i$. At $A=B$, $g=u$, the last two displayed equalities and the definition in step 5 give $$c_{i+1}^{E_1}\delta_E^i=(\delta_E^i\otimes1)c_i^{E_3}.$$ This includes every connecting map; step 7 includes the other maps. Together with the natural long exact sequence of [pqf-def-cohomology] this proves the last assertion. None of the steps required properness, finite-dimensional cohomology, smoothness or reductivity.
